clue.text: Are mostly the French found in this town?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word Are is used, dropping its final letter

parts.note: les is the French plural word for 'the'

explanation.surface: A question asking whether most of the French are to be found in some particular town.
explanation.walkthrough: ARLES is a town in Provence, southern France, so 'the French' fits the surface neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Arles is a historic town in Provence, famed for its Roman arena and for Van Gogh.

clue.text: Like one key part of the East

parts.note: as means like, in the sense 'just as'
I is the Roman numeral for one
A minor is a musical key

explanation.surface: Something described as resembling a single important region of the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor, roughly modern Anatolia, is a region at the western edge of Asia, the East to Europeans.

clue.text: Permits, we hear, provided for Soviet group

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for permits is to be spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: lets means permits or allows

explanation.surface: Something about permissions granted to a group within the old Soviet Union.
explanation.walkthrough: When this was set, Latvia was part of the USSR, so the Latvian people were a Soviet group.
explanation.definitionFit: Letts are the people of Latvia, then a republic of the Soviet Union.

clue.text: It makes sheep itch to graze around the island

indicators.note: around means the word for graze goes about the island's letter

parts.note: to graze the skin is to scrape it
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A warning that sheep scratch themselves while grazing round an island pasture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'graze' pretends to be about sheep eating; here it means to scrape.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrapie is a fatal brain disease of sheep that causes intense itching, so they scrape against fences.

clue.text: Piece of luggage on train? One may unpack it in first class

definitions.text: One may unpack it in first class

indicators.note: on means one piece follows the other in this across entry, the luggage coming after

parts.note: to school a person is to train them
a bag is an item of luggage

explanation.surface: A railway passenger with a case aboard the train, opened up in a first-class carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first class' suggests a railway carriage but means the first lesson of the school day; 'train' is the verb meaning teach.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil carries books in a satchel and empties it at the start of the opening lesson.

clue.text: Top of strut needs wing-shaped screw

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of strut, since this is a down entry read from the top

parts.note: alary is a technical adjective meaning relating to or shaped like wings

explanation.surface: Workshop instructions: a wing-nut style screw is needed at the top of a strut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screw' looks like a piece of hardware, but it is slang for pay, as in 'on a good screw'.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is informal British slang for wages, the regular pay for a job.

clue.text: Ambassador takes a chance in the airport

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title given to an ambassador
a throw is a go or chance, as in 'ten pounds a throw'

explanation.surface: A diplomat gambling while waiting in an airport terminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's main international airport.

clue.text: For example, second service book

explanation.surface: An example of a second prayer book used at church services.
explanation.definitionFit: Second is an example of an ordinal number; an ordinal is also the book of forms for ordaining clergy.

clue.text: American stars found in amusement park

explanation.surface: American celebrities spotted at a theme park.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the Plough constellation the Big Dipper; in Britain a big dipper is also a roller coaster ride.

clue.text: Fare required to board vehicle

explanation.surface: A passenger needs the fare in order to climb aboard a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: To fare is to progress or manage, as in 'how are you managing'; to board a bus is to climb aboard it.

clue.text: Amongst others put in grave situation, otherwise cut

parts.note: to inter is to bury, putting a body in a grave

indicators.note: cut means the word for otherwise loses its final letter

parts.note: alias means otherwise, as in 'otherwise known as'

explanation.surface: Placed among others in a serious predicament, or else wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' reads as serious but is the burial place; 'cut' drops the last letter of ALIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter alia is Latin for among other things, used to show a list is not complete.

clue.text: Appreciate it could be a bit of a handful

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking or appreciating it

explanation.surface: Admitting that something might prove a little difficult to manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a handful' suggests trouble, but it is literally the hand, of which a finger is one bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A finger is one part of the hand, so a fingertip-sized piece of what a hand holds.

clue.text: Failure to understand, perhaps, mine is no different

indicators.note: different means the letters of the preceding words are made into something else

explanation.surface: Someone protests that a mere misunderstanding is no different from theirs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges the fifteen letters of PERHAPS MINE IS NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A misunderstanding is a mistaken belief, a failure to grasp what was meant.

clue.text: One who takes note no longer

explanation.surface: A person who collects banknotes that are no longer in use.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for steal, so a thief; a nicker was also old slang for a pound note.

clue.text: Spotted below, holding one's own cutter

indicators.note: below means in this down entry the word for spotted comes underneath the other part

parts.note: coping means managing, holding one's own
saw is the past tense of see, meaning spotted

explanation.surface: Someone noticed underneath, keeping a blade or knife for themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A coping saw is a fine-bladed tool for cutting curves in wood.

clue.text: Sweet sort of man giving children guidance

definitions.text: sort of man giving children guidance

explanation.surface: A kindly man who guides children, perhaps with sweets in his pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: A lollipop is a sweet on a stick; a lollipop man is the British school crossing warden with a round sign.

clue.text: Political activist, one involved with social affairs

parts.note: party, as in a political party
a goer is an energetic, active person

explanation.surface: A political campaigner who is also busy with social issues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social affairs' sounds political but means parties and gatherings.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who attends parties is involved in social occasions.

clue.text: Greets unusual form of clue — upset some, possibly

indicators.note: upset means the letters are knocked over and rearranged
unusual form of means the word clue is altered, its U becoming a W, the double U

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A puzzle setter's odd clue greets solvers and might annoy some of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual form of' changes CLUE to CLWE (W being a 'double U'); 'upset' then rearranges CLWE with SOME.
explanation.definitionFit: To welcome someone is to greet them warmly on arrival.

clue.text: State sent letters immediately answered

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
posted means sent letters by mail

explanation.surface: A statement that someone dispatched letters which received an instant reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a verb, but it is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: To riposte is to make a quick retort, so a swift reply.

clue.text: Leak in interview with some paper

parts.note: to see someone can mean to interview or consult them
a page is a portion of paper

explanation.surface: A news leak given during an interview to part of the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is liquid slowly escaping through small gaps.

clue.text: Car takes new route, heading right

indicators.note: new means the word route is made into a fresh arrangement
heading means the first letter of right

explanation.surface: A driver takes a new road and turns right.
explanation.definitionFit: A tourer is an open touring car built for long journeys.

clue.text: Sinister contents of some tiny house

indicators.note: contents of means the inner letters of each of the three words, without their outer letters

explanation.surface: Something ominous lurking inside a small cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contents of' takes the middle of each word: OM from some, IN from tiny, OUS from house.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means threatening, giving a sense that something bad is coming.

clue.text: Green party finally contrived to get power

indicators.note: contrived means the letters of Green are reworked into a new order
finally means the last letter of party

explanation.surface: The Green Party has at last schemed its way into power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green party' reads as the political party, but the words split into anagram fodder and a final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Energy is the capacity to do work, which a physicist calls power.

clue.text: Bashful about name-dropping, left in patronising way

indicators.note: about means the word for bashful is placed around the other letters

parts.note: coy means shy or bashful
descending means going down, dropping

explanation.surface: A shy person ashamed of name-dropping is left looking haughty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'name-dropping' looks like boasting about famous acquaintances, but 'dropping' means going down; 'about' puts the shy word round everything else, and 'in' sits with the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting condescendingly means behaving with an air of superiority towards others.

clue.text: Numbers of Romans are so polite

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
VI is 6 in Roman numerals
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A claim that Roman citizens were famously courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter of the answer is a Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil means courteous, showing basic good manners.

clue.text: Foolish person accepts sovereign for old coin

indicators.note: accepts means the word for foolish person takes the other letter inside

parts.note: a goat is informal for a fool, as in 'acting the goat'
R is for Rex or Regina, king or queen

explanation.surface: A gullible person takes a gold sovereign in payment for an antique coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' suggests the gold coin, but it is the monarch, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A groat was an old English silver coin worth four pence.

clue.text: Prospect of Eastenders breaking through

indicators.note: breaking means the letters break into the word for through

parts.note: via means by way of, through
the enders, last two letters, of the word East

explanation.surface: The outlook for the BBC soap EastEnders breaking through.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a British TV soap, but here it is read as 'East-enders', the end letters of East.
explanation.definitionFit: A vista is a view stretching into the distance, a prospect.

clue.text: Company restricted by spoilsport in Merchant of Venice

indicators.note: restricted by means the company letters are held within the other part

parts.note: split as spoil, giving mar, and sport, giving polo

explanation.surface: A firm hampered by a killjoy in Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merchant of Venice' is Shakespeare's play title, but here it describes the explorer, a Venetian trader.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was a Venetian trader whose travels to China made him famous.

clue.text: Impeccably removing head, in illegal fashion

indicators.note: removing head means the first letter is cut off the word for impeccably

parts.note: flawlessly means impeccably, without any fault

explanation.surface: Beheading someone perfectly, but against the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawlessly means without regard for the rules, unlawfully.

clue.text: Instrument I put in, following top performer's lead

indicators.note: put in means the I goes inside the word for top performer

parts.note: a star is the leading performer

explanation.surface: A musician inserting a part, following the star soloist's lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following ... lead' places I straight after S, the lead letter of STAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitar is a long-necked Indian stringed lute.
